notes: Parts are unchanged from step 1; no part was added or dropped.

Circuit: 5V -> red wire -> + rail -> orange wire -> button column 4 (side 1). Button column 6 (side 2) -> teal wire to Arduino pin 2, and also -> 10k resistor -> column 9 -> short black wire -> GND rail -> black wire -> Arduino GND. This matches the schematic: pin 2 sits between the button and the pull-down resistor.

The breadboard image is drawn with rows j-f at the top and e-a at the bottom. The catalogue calls rows a-e bank 't' and rows f-j bank 'b'. So the lower half of the image is bank 't' and the rails next to it are 'tp' (+, lower line) and 'tn' (-, upper line).
Rail hole numbers (tp.1, tp.3, tn.1, tn.8) only record roughly where each wire sits. Each rail is one strip, so the numbers don't change the connectivity.

The button straddles the centre gap with legs in columns 4 and 6. I took the two legs in the same column (top and bottom of the gap) to be the internally joined pair. Side 1 is column 4 (1.l = 4b.f, 1.r = 4t.e). Side 2 is column 6 (2.l = 6b.f, 2.r = 6t.e).
The black wire goes to the GND pin on the Uno power header. I mapped it to GND.1, since the image doesn't say which GND pin it is. All Uno GND pins are the same net.
The LED on pin 13 is the Arduino's built-in LED, so no external LED is built.
